title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: single-trail Nivasch-stack rho in GT

claims.statement: For a uniform nonidentity P in BLS12-381 G1 and an independent uniform z in GT, the attack in proof.md returns Q=[a]Q0 in G2 with e(P,Q)=z under the pinned pairing convention, using at most 2^127.95 total target-group-operation equivalents (dense Fp12 multiplications, C=20,000), with success probability at least 0.42 from the standard random-mapping model ALONE. It computes g=e(P,Q0) (a generator) and solves z=g^a by a SINGLE-TRAIL R-adding Pollard rho on GT with NIVASCH SINGLE-STACK cycle detection: one continuous trajectory F^i(X_0), F(X)=X*M_{H(X)} with R=2^20 adding entries, costs ONE dense Fp12 multiplication per step (no tortoise/hare 3x factor). Detection uses a FIXED TOTAL ORDER on the exact element encoding (the integer formed by the 12 reduced tower coefficients, injective on GT, so key-equality IFF element-equality -- NO distinguished-point predicate, NO fingerprint, NO coefficient-bit density or equidistribution assumption, NO pseudorandom function). The Nivasch stack holds the RIGHT-TO-LEFT (suffix) minima of the key sequence (each X_j with key less than every later element up to the current step; for successive keys 3,1,2 the stack is [1,2]); the walk detects its self-collision EXACTLY at the second occurrence of the cycle-minimum element, at step D=p+lambda with mu+lambda<=D<mu+2*lambda<=2*rho, yielding a=(A_j-A_D)/(B_D-B_j) mod r. H=bits 0..19 of the first tower coefficient only selects an adding entry (its balance is subsumed in the random-mapping model, irrelevant to detection/memory). Table exponents are the rules' fresh uniform algorithm coins (512 bits mod r, bias<2^-256). The stack size is the number of right-to-left (suffix) minima = backward records, expected ~ln t ~88 at t~2^127 under the random-mapping order (same law as the record count). It is O(log) native memory in ONE machine (<2^64 bytes): a hard cap of 2^40 entries, each key (576 bytes) + (A,B) (64 bytes) + a 16-BYTE index (128-bit, since the budget is ~2^128 steps) <=2^10 bytes = <=2^50 bytes, Chernoff-negligible overflow-to-counted-failure; NO distributed storage, NO routing. Budget T=ceil(1.30*k0) (k0=sqrt(2*r*ln(1/0.61))): under the random-mapping model the detection step D=rho*(1+V*(1-U)) with U,V~Unif[0,1] (tail/cycle split index uniform; cycle-minimum position uniform by exchangeability; rho tail exp(-t^2/2r)), so P(D<=T)=1-E[exp(-1.30^2*ln(1/0.61)/(1+V(1-U))^2)]=0.431, giving success>=0.42>=0.39 after negligible deductions. A deterministic ceiling D<2*rho holds for every trajectory (no cycle-min-position assumption), so detection always occurs by step 2*rho (this bounds the stack horizon); this is NOT an unconditional success bound -- converting it to a success probability still uses the random-mapping collision-time law, under which budget 2*k0 gives success>=P(rho<=k0)>=0.39 (time_log2~128.45), a model-conditional fallback. No part of the claim is asserted to hold independently of the single random-mapping model. Cost uses an explicit AArch64 instruction-level ledger charged at FULL worst-case key length (NO short-prefix assumption): a 3-way compare of two 64-bit key words = 6 instr (2 loads, CMP, branch, 2 address/loop); amortized pop-comparisons <=T + stopping comparison T (its 3-way result also decides detect/push, no separate equality compare) = <=2T comparisons * 72 words * 6 = <=864T; pushes <=T copying 82 words at 3 instr/word +control = <=250T; pops ~2T; per-step H(12)+two 255-bit modular exponent adds(40)+adding-entry setup(20)+128-bit index incr(3) = ~75T; total non-mult <=1191T instr = 0.0596T units, so total work <=T*(1+0.0596)=T*1.0596 units (amortized/total instruction bound). W=1.30*k0*1.0596=2^127.882, rounded up to 2^127.95. Peak memory <=2^50 bytes native (reported only; stack access charged in the 1.0284 units). Preprocessing (2^20-entry table) <=2^31 units included; nonuniform advice 0 bytes. The experiment runs the REAL Nivasch stack and measures the detection-budget success distribution on an abstract random mapping AND a real F_p* subgroup R-adding walk: 100% correct self-collision detection, E[D/rho]=1.27 (predicted 1.25), P(D<=1.30*k0)=0.43 (abstract) and ~0.40 (real group, q~2^20, R=64, one carried exponent) CONSISTENT with the integral, max stack 21 (~log2 state size), 120/120 exact detections on real group elements. These are EXPLORATORY confirmations at feasible sizes, not a production-scale identity of distributions; transfer to the GT representation and R=2^20 is a heuristic extrapolation under the single random-mapping model (as for the accepted collision-time law). Single-processor (serial; score processor-count independent). Classical cold attack, no uncharged advice or quantum steps; generic square-root accounting, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Validate the SUBMITTED algorithm's collision and detection behavior. (A) On random mappings (the accepted rho heuristic), run the real Nivasch single-stack detection and measure: exact-detection correctness (fraction of runs whose stack match is a genuine self-collision), the detection-stretch law D=rho*(1+V(1-U)) via E[D/rho] (predicted 1.25), the success fraction P(D<=beta*k0) at the submitted budget beta=1.30 (predicted 0.431), and the maximum stack size (~log2 of the state size, confirming native O(log) memory). (B) On a real prime-order-q subgroup of F_p*, run an R-adding walk keyed by the element's integer value and confirm exact self-collision detection and that the recovered exponents satisfy the collision relation. No distinguished-point density or coefficient-bit equidistribution is used anywhere.
